facts.raw_span: A 20-year-old woman was being monitored for a left ciliary body mass for 3 years presented with declining vision in her left eye
Her best-corrected visual acuity was 20/20 OD and 20/50 OS
Pupils, intraocular pressures, anterior chambers, and lenses were unremarkable in both eyes
a nasal mass posterior to the lens was evident, which had grown considerably in size since her last visit
Ophthalmoscopic examination showed a large white mass protruding into the vitreous cavity
Ultra-widefield imaging: White mass emanating anteriorly from the nasal ciliary body and protruding into the vitreous cavity
Vitreous aspirate cytology: Negative for malignant cells
Hypovascular myxoid lesion composed of loosely arranged spindle and stellate cells with spindle nuclei
S100 (neural crest marker): Positive
Glial fibrillary acidic protein (astrocyte marker): Patchy positive
CD34 (fibroblast marker): Negative
Smooth muscle actin: Negative
A 20-year-old woman was being monitored for a left ciliary body mass for 3 years presented with declining vision in her left eye
Her best-corrected visual acuity was 20/20 OD and 20/50 OS
Pupils, intraocular pressures, anterior chambers, and lenses were unremarkable in both eyes
a nasal mass posterior to the lens was evident, which had grown considerably in size since her last visit
Ophthalmoscopic examination showed a large white mass protruding into the vitreous cavity
Ultra-widefield imaging: White mass emanating anteriorly from the nasal ciliary body and protruding into the vitreous cavity
Vitreous aspirate cytology: Negative for malignant cells
Hypovascular myxoid lesion composed of loosely arranged spindle and stellate cells with spindle nuclei
S100 (neural crest marker): Positive
Glial fibrillary acidic protein (astrocyte marker): Patchy positive
CD34 (fibroblast marker): Negative
Smooth muscle actin: Negative

concepts.why: The presence of a nasal mass posterior to the lens, which has grown considerably in size, along with the ophthalmoscopic examination showing a large white mass protruding into the vitreous cavity, and the histopathological findings of a hypovascular myxoid lesion composed of loosely arranged spindle and stellate cells, suggest a diagnosis of Medulloepithelioma.
The patient's history of being monitored for a left ciliary body mass and the current findings of a nasal mass posterior to the lens suggest a ciliary body tumor.
The positive S100 staining and the presence of glial fibrillary acidic protein suggest a neuroepithelial origin of the tumor.
The histopathological findings of a hypovascular myxoid lesion suggest a myxoid tumor.
The negative results for malignant cells, CD34, and smooth muscle actin, along with the positive S100 staining, are consistent with a diagnosis of neurofibroma, a type of benign nerve sheath tumor.
